name: Rosacea
description: Rosacea is a common skin condition that causes redness and visible blood vessels in the face. It can also lead to bumps, pimples, and burning or stinging sensations.
causes: Environmental triggers (such as sun exposure, hot weather, cold wind)
Certain foods and beverages (chocolate, alcohol, spicy food)
symptoms: Bumps and pimples similar to acne but not inflamed or filled with pus
risk_factors: Living in a hot, humid climate
Having certain medical conditions such as rhinitis and blepharitis
Being between the ages of 30 and 50
ingredients_to_avoid: Essential oils (except for chamomile in low concentration)

daily_routine.purpose: Remove dirt and oil from the skin without irritating it.
Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen daily to protect against UV radiation.
Maintain skin hydration which can help reduce redness and irritation.

natural_remedies: Applying cool compresses to soothe the skin
Using a humidifier in dry weather conditions
Avoiding triggers such as spicy foods and hot beverages
lifestyle_tips: Maintaining a healthy diet and avoiding known dietary triggers
common_myths: Rosacea can be cured with antibiotics.
when_to_consult_doctor: Seek medical advice if you notice persistent redness, bumps, or other symptoms that do not resolve on their own within a week or two of appearing.
prevention: Avoiding known triggers such as sunlight and spicy foods
Using gentle skincare products without alcohol or fragrances

severity_levels.mild: Persistent redness, occasional flushing, mild papules (small bumps) or pustules (pus-filled bumps)
severity_levels.moderate: Visible blood vessels, more frequent flushing, and more pronounced skin irritation
severity_levels.severe: Erythema (extensive redness), telangiectasia (widened blood vessels), plaques (flat, red patches of skin), rhinophyma (an enlarged, bulbous nose)

expert_tips: Keep a detailed diary to track what triggers your rosacea
Regularly consult with a dermatologist for personalized treatment plans
